    Known Direct Subclasses:
    AttributeList ， RoleList ， RoleUnresolvedList 
    public class ArrayList<E>
extends AbstractList<E>
implements List<E>, RandomAccess, Cloneable, Serializable
    ListResizable array implementation of the interface. Implements all optional list operations and permits all elements, includingnull 。 except implementationListIn addition to the interface, this class also provides some methods to manipulate the size of the array used internally to store the list. (This class is roughly equivalent toVector, except that it is not synchronized.)

    thatsize ， isEmpty ， get ， set ， iteratorandlistIteratorThe operation runs in constant time. addoperates inamortized constant timeruns, that is, adding n elements requires O(n) time. All other operations run in linear time (roughly speaking). andLinkedListCompared with the implementation, the constant factor is lower.

    eachArrayListeach instance has aCapacity 。 The capacity is the size of the array used to store the elements in the list. It is always at least as large as the list size. As elements are added to an ArrayList, its capacity automatically increases. Other than the fact that adding elements has constant amortized time cost, the details of the growth strategy are not specified.

    When usingensureCapacityBefore an operation adds a large number of elements, the application can increaseArrayListthe capacity of the instance. This may reduce the number of incremental reallocations.

    Note that this implementation is not synchronized. If multiple threads access simultaneouslyArrayListinstance, and at least one thread has structurally modified the list, thenRequiredSynchronize externally. （StructuremodifyYesaddorDeleteaor multipleelement'sanyOperation, or显formula调整BackuparrayofSize;onlySettingselement'sThe value is notStructuremodify。）这通常Throughsame步one些自butEncapsulationobject ofto implement.name单。 If such an object does not exist, you should useCollections.synchronizedListThe method “wraps” the list. This is best done at creation time, to prevent accidental unsynchronized access to the list: 

      List list = Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList(...));

    This type ofiteratorandlistIteratorThe iterator returned by the method isfail-fast: if the list is structurally modified at any time after the iterator is created, except through the iterator's ownremoveoraddExcept through the method, the iterator will throwConcurrentModificationException 。 Therefore, in the case of concurrent modification, the iterator fails fast and cleanly, rather than risking arbitrary, non-deterministic behavior at an unspecified time in the future.

    Please note that the fail-fast behavior of iterators cannot be guaranteed, because in general, it is impossible to make any hard guarantees in the presence of unsynchronized concurrent modification. Fail-fast iterators throw on a best-effort basisConcurrentModificationException 。 Therefore, it is incorrect to write programs that depend on this exception to ensure their correctness:The fail-fast behavior of an iterator should be used only to detect bugs.

      • toArray

        public Object[] toArray()
        Returns an array containing all elements in this list in proper order (from the first element to the last element).

        The returned array will be "safe" because this list does not retain references to it. (In other words, this method must allocate a new array). Thus the caller is free to modify the returned array.

        This method acts as a bridge between array-based and collection-based APIs.

      • toArray

        public <T> T[] toArray​(T[] a)
        Returns an array containing all elements in this list in proper order (from the first element to the last element); The runtime type of the returned array is the runtime type of the specified array. If the list fits in the specified array, it is returned therein. Otherwise, a new array is allocated with the runtime type of the specified array and the size of this list.

        If the list fits in the specified array with room to spare (i.e., the array has more elements than the list), the element in the array immediately following the end of the collection is set tonull 。 （ onlyWhen the caller knows that the list does not contain any null elements, this is useful in determining the length of the list.)

      • subList

        public List<E> subList​(int fromIndex,
                       int toIndex)
        Returns the specifiedfromIndex(inclusive) andtoIndexA view of the portion of this list between (exclusive). (iffromIndexandtoIndexIf equal, the returned list is empty.) The returned list is backed by this list, so non-structural changes in the returned list are reflected in this list, and vice versa. The returned list supports all optional list operations.

        This method eliminates the need for explicit range operations (of the sort that commonly exist for arrays). Any operation that expects a list can be used as a range operation by passing a subList view instead of a whole list. For example, the following idiom removes a range of elements from a list: 

          list.subList(from, to).clear();
        can beindexOf(Object)andlastIndexOf(Object)Constructs a similar idiom, and canCollectionsAll algorithms in the class apply to sublists.

        If the backing list (i.e., this list) is instructurallyin any way other than through the returned listVariablethen the semantics of the list returned by this method become undefined. (Structural modifications are those that change the size of this list, or otherwise disturb it in ways that an ongoing iteration may produce incorrect results.)

        Specified by:
        subList, interfaceList<E>
        Override:
        subListin the courseAbstractList<E>
        Parameter

        toIndex - toIndexThe high endpoint (exclusive)
        Result
        A view of the specified range within this list
        Exception
        IndexOutOfBoundsException- If the endpoint index values are out of range(fromIndex < 0 || toIndex > size)
        IllegalArgumentException- If the endpoint indices are out of order(fromIndex > toIndex)
